subject: English Language
title: Conjunctions
introduction: Join ideas clearly, then practise five questions at a time.

rules.title: Join ideas and show meaning
rules.body: And adds; but or although contrasts; because gives a reason; so that shows purpose. Use because before a clause and because of before a noun phrase.
rules.example: She stayed home because she was ill. · Although she was ill, she studied.

rules.title: Time, place and condition
rules.body: When, while, until and as soon as tell us about time. Wherever refers to place. If introduces a condition; unless means if not.
rules.example: Wait until I return. · Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.

rules.title: Paired conjunctions
rules.body: Use either…or and neither…nor as pairs. Keep the joined parts in the same grammatical form.
rules.example: She will choose either pasta or noodles. · Neither Ravi nor Meera was late.

rules.title: The inversion pairs
rules.body: After no sooner, use than. After hardly, scarcely or barely, use when. These often use inverted word order.
rules.example: No sooner had I arrived than it rained. · Hardly had I arrived when it rained.

worked.prompt: The road was slippery. The driver managed to control the car.
worked.answer: Although the road was slippery, the driver managed to control the car.
worked.explanation: Although shows that the second event happened despite the first.

questions.prompt: The road was slippery. The driver managed to control the car.
questions.answer: Although the road was slippery, the driver managed to control the car.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The book is fascinating. It contains several historical illustrations.
questions.answer: The book, which contains several historical illustrations, is fascinating.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: You must apologise. The teacher will not forgive your mistake.
questions.answer: Unless you apologise, the teacher will not forgive your mistake.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: You eat too much. You will feel sick.
questions.answer: If you eat too much, you will feel sick.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The chef will prepare pasta. The chef will prepare noodles.
questions.answer: The chef will prepare either pasta or noodles.
accepted: Either the chef will prepare pasta or noodles.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The detective found no evidence at the crime scene. He found no witnesses to the incident.
questions.answer: The detective found neither evidence at the crime scene nor witnesses to the incident.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The athlete crossed the finish line. The crowd began cheering immediately.
questions.answer: Hardly had the athlete crossed the finish line when the crowd began cheering.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The principal announced the results. The students started celebrating immediately.
questions.answer: No sooner had the principal announced the results than the students started celebrating.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The weather was very cold. The children continued playing outside.
questions.answer: Although the weather was very cold, the children continued playing outside.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: The shopkeeper did not have the blue dress. He did not have the green dress.
questions.answer: The shopkeeper had neither the blue dress nor the green dress.
questions.explanation: Use a suitable connector while keeping the original meaning. Do not use and, but or so.

questions.prompt: ___ you work carefully, you may make avoidable mistakes.
questions.answer: Unless
questions.explanation: Unless means if not.

questions.prompt: We stayed indoors ___ the storm had passed.
questions.answer: until
questions.explanation: Until marks the end of a period.

questions.prompt: ___ the bell rang, the pupils entered the hall immediately.
questions.answer: As soon as
questions.explanation: As soon as shows immediate sequence.

questions.prompt: ___ he was exhausted, he completed the race.
questions.answer: Although
questions.explanation: Although introduces a contrast.

questions.prompt: The library closed early ___ the librarian was ill.
questions.answer: because
questions.explanation: Because introduces a reason.

questions.prompt: I shall call you ___ I reach home.
questions.answer: when
questions.explanation: When links actions in time.

questions.prompt: ___ you travel, carry your identity card.
questions.answer: Wherever
questions.explanation: Wherever means in any place that.

questions.prompt: She spoke softly ___ the baby could sleep.
questions.answer: so that
questions.explanation: So that introduces purpose.

questions.prompt: He read quietly ___ his sister practised the piano.
questions.answer: while
questions.explanation: While shows simultaneous action.

questions.prompt: You may choose ___ tea or coffee.
questions.answer: either
questions.explanation: Either pairs with or.

questions.prompt: Neither the captain ___ the coach was satisfied.
questions.answer: nor
questions.explanation: Neither pairs with nor.

questions.prompt: No sooner had the show begun ___ the lights went out.
questions.answer: than
questions.explanation: No sooner pairs with than.

questions.prompt: Hardly had I sat down ___ the telephone rang.
questions.answer: when
questions.explanation: Hardly pairs with when.

questions.prompt: She is taller ___ her older sister.
questions.answer: than
questions.explanation: Than makes this comparison.

questions.prompt: We could not go out ___ it was raining heavily.
questions.answer: because
questions.explanation: Because is followed by a clause.

questions.prompt: We could not go out ___ the heavy rain.
questions.answer: because of
questions.explanation: Because of is followed by a noun phrase.

questions.prompt: ___ you leave now, you will catch the train.
questions.answer: If
questions.explanation: If introduces the condition.

questions.prompt: We waited ___ the teacher returned.
questions.answer: until
questions.explanation: Until marks the end of waiting.

questions.prompt: ___ it was late, they continued studying.
questions.answer: Although
questions.explanation: Although shows unexpected contrast.

questions.prompt: He took notes ___ he would remember the details.
questions.answer: so that
questions.explanation: So that introduces purpose.

questions.prompt: I will read ___ you prepare dinner.
questions.answer: while
questions.explanation: While links simultaneous actions.

questions.prompt: You may go ___ you wish.
questions.answer: wherever
questions.explanation: Wherever refers to place.

questions.prompt: She opened the door ___ the bell rang.
questions.answer: as soon as
questions.explanation: As soon as shows an immediate action.

questions.prompt: He remained calm ___ everyone else panicked.
questions.answer: whereas
questions.explanation: Whereas contrasts two situations.

questions.prompt: ___ you finish your work, you may leave.
questions.answer: Once
questions.explanation: Once means after something happens.

questions.prompt: ___ had we reached the station than the train arrived.
questions.answer: No sooner
questions.explanation: No sooner pairs with than.

questions.prompt: ___ had the rain stopped when the players returned.
questions.answer: Scarcely
questions.explanation: Scarcely pairs with when.

questions.prompt: You can ___ revise now or practise tomorrow.
questions.answer: either
questions.explanation: Either pairs with or.

questions.prompt: ___ my brother nor my sister likes the film.
questions.answer: Neither
questions.explanation: Neither pairs with nor.

questions.prompt: Wait here ___ I come back.
questions.answer: until
questions.explanation: Until marks the time when waiting ends.

questions.prompt: Mira revised the chapter. She explained it to her friends. (Use: not only ... but also)
questions.starter: Mira revised the chapter. She explained it to her friends.
questions.answer: Mira not only revised the chapter but also explained it to her friends.
questions.explanation: Both actions belong to Mira; keep the verbs parallel.

questions.prompt: You submit the form today. You will miss the competition. (Use: unless)
questions.starter: You submit the form today. You will miss the competition.
questions.answer: Unless you submit the form today, you will miss the competition.
questions.explanation: Unless means if not.

questions.prompt: The evidence was incomplete. The jury reached a decision. (Use: although)
questions.starter: The evidence was incomplete. The jury reached a decision.
questions.answer: Although the evidence was incomplete, the jury reached a decision.
questions.explanation: Although shows an unexpected contrast.

questions.prompt: We can travel by train. We can travel by bus. (Use: either ... or)
questions.starter: We can travel by train. We can travel by bus.
questions.answer: We can travel either by train or by bus.
questions.explanation: Either...or presents alternatives.

questions.prompt: Anika did not complain. Anika did not give up. (Use: neither ... nor)
questions.starter: Anika did not complain. Anika did not give up.
questions.answer: Anika neither complained nor gave up.
questions.explanation: Neither...nor joins two negative ideas without another negative.

questions.prompt: The bell rang. The students entered the hall. (Use: as soon as)
questions.starter: The bell rang. The students entered the hall.
questions.answer: As soon as the bell rang, the students entered the hall.
questions.explanation: As soon as shows immediate sequence.

questions.prompt: You may borrow my notes. You return them tomorrow. (Use: provided that)
questions.starter: You may borrow my notes. You return them tomorrow.
questions.answer: You may borrow my notes provided that you return them tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Provided that introduces a condition.

questions.prompt: The first plan saves time. The second plan saves money. (Use: whereas)
questions.starter: The first plan saves time. The second plan saves money.
questions.answer: The first plan saves time, whereas the second plan saves money.
questions.explanation: Whereas contrasts two plans.

questions.prompt: The guests arrived. The lights went out immediately. (Use: no sooner ... than)
questions.starter: The guests arrived. The lights went out immediately.
questions.answer: No sooner had the guests arrived than the lights went out.
questions.explanation: No sooner pairs with than and uses inversion here.

questions.prompt: The match started. Rain interrupted it immediately. (Use: hardly ... when)
questions.starter: The match started. Rain interrupted it immediately.
questions.answer: Hardly had the match started when rain interrupted it.
questions.explanation: Hardly pairs with when and uses inversion here.

questions.prompt: The teacher repeated the instructions. Everyone could understand them. (Use: so that)
questions.starter: The teacher repeated the instructions. Everyone could understand them.
questions.answer: The teacher repeated the instructions so that everyone could understand them.
questions.explanation: So that expresses purpose.

questions.prompt: The team will practise. The weather may be sunny or rainy. (Use: whether ... or)
questions.starter: The team will practise. The weather may be sunny or rainy.
questions.answer: The team will practise whether the weather is sunny or rainy.
questions.explanation: Whether...or covers both possibilities.

questions.prompt: The guard waited. The last visitor left. (Use: until)
questions.starter: The guard waited. The last visitor left.
questions.answer: The guard waited until the last visitor left.
questions.explanation: Until marks when the waiting ended.

questions.prompt: The puzzle looked simple. Few students solved it. (Use: even though)
questions.starter: The puzzle looked simple. Few students solved it.
questions.answer: Even though the puzzle looked simple, few students solved it.
questions.explanation: Even though highlights an unexpected result.

questions.prompt: The museum displays paintings. The museum displays sculptures. (Use: both ... and)
questions.starter: The museum displays paintings. The museum displays sculptures.
questions.answer: The museum displays both paintings and sculptures.
questions.explanation: Both...and includes each item.

questions.prompt: The hikers carried a map. They might lose their way. (Use: lest)
questions.starter: The hikers carried a map. They might lose their way.
questions.answer: The hikers carried a map lest they should lose their way.
questions.explanation: Lest expresses prevention; lest...should is formal usage.

questions.prompt: Take a torch. The electricity may fail. (Use: in case)
questions.starter: Take a torch. The electricity may fail.
questions.answer: Take a torch in case the electricity fails.
questions.explanation: In case prepares for a possibility.

questions.prompt: She chose to verify the claim. She did not repeat the rumour. (Use: rather than)
questions.starter: She chose to verify the claim. She did not repeat the rumour.
questions.answer: She chose to verify the claim rather than repeat the rumour.
questions.explanation: Rather than shows the preferred action.

questions.prompt: You may use the library. You keep it quiet. (Use: as long as)
questions.starter: You may use the library. You keep it quiet.
questions.answer: You may use the library as long as you keep it quiet.
questions.explanation: As long as introduces a continuing condition.

questions.prompt: The storm damaged the roof. It flooded the garden. (Use: not only ... but also)
questions.starter: The storm damaged the roof. It flooded the garden.
questions.answer: The storm not only damaged the roof but also flooded the garden.
questions.explanation: Not only...but also links parallel verbs.
